summary: BUG-0043: phase1 and installer had failed on every Gitea run since 2026-09-08 because the runner executes jobs in an unprivileged container. phase1 stopped at an unshare step that ran sixth, skipping the 18 checks after it; installer bind-mounted a path that does not exist on the Docker host. phase1 now runs every unprivileged check first and gates the namespace steps on a detected capability with a loud warning naming the missing coverage. The Gitea installer job was scoped to what that runner can do: source checks and regressions run directly in the job container, and four checks were DELETED — native bridge, DHCP preview, ISO build with initramfs completeness, and wizard/progress. That job no longer establishes an ISO is buildable and warns so on every run. The GitHub copy keeps the full matrix. API impact: none — CI configuration only. The release workflow gained the same bind-mount preflight, since it builds the ISO the same way and would otherwise fail deep inside the build, and the release guide documents that blocker. Follow-up: Gitea executes .github/workflows, not .gitea/workflows, so two pushes that scoped only the .gitea installer changed nothing and .gitea/workflows/release.yml would never have fired. Both installer files are now identical and release.yml exists in both. Third pass: phase1 then reached 20 of 24 steps and failed at the local host browser check, which runs docker with the same container-only workspace mount; the two libvirt steps after it need KVM. The separate probes were replaced by one hostcap step testing both namespace creation and a Docker bind mount, and all five host-dependent steps are gated on it.

guide.reason: The release guide now states that releases are blocked: the runner cannot bind-mount the workspace, so no workflow builds an ISO and a release must be built and published by hand. Its Status and Verification sections previously implied CI produced the ISO. The rest of this change is contributor CI configuration with no operator-facing behaviour.

api.reason: Workflow step ordering and gating only. No Controller operation, agent command, event, stream, observed-state flow or client-facing endpoint is added, removed or changed, and no product source file is touched by this change.

state.reason: Build, packaging, CI or release tooling only; no Nex Controller or Core state.

verification.method: bash installer/check.sh and all seven tests/integration/installer-*.py checks plus the installer-network.c compile-and-run were executed on a workstation outside any container, exactly as the scoped job invokes them: all nine pass, confirming they never needed the builder image. All seven workflow files parsed with PyYAML; phase1 step order confirmed as go test, contract/unit checks, UI build, advisories, then the capability probe followed by the two gated namespace steps carrying if: steps.netns.outputs.available == 'true'. Audited every run: block across .gitea and .github for ${{ }} interpolation and found none. Root cause read from the failing runs: job 4335 shows 'bash: installer/check.sh: No such file or directory' after -v "$PWD:/work"; job 4336 shows 'unshare: unshare failed: Operation not permitted' with go test -race ./... already passed and 18 steps skipped; job 4338 confirms $PWD is /workspace/stocky789/Nex, a container-only path. Gitea run history shows phase1 and installer failing on every run from 2026-09-08, predating these changes. NOT verified: no run was triggered after scoping, so the reordered and scoped pipelines have not executed; the docker build step was not exercised locally. ISO build, bridge, DHCP, initramfs, wizard and namespace coverage are OUTSTANDING, deleted or skipped rather than restored, and need a host-mode runner label. Third pass evidence: run 3789 job 4354 shows 20 of 24 steps passing — including the unit tests, contract check, UI build, advisories and every browser workflow — and failing only at 'Verify local host browser authentication and preflight blockers' with cc1: fatal error on /workspace/stocky789/Nex/packaging/core-local/nex-root-auth.c, a file that exists and is tracked; tests/integration/localcore_browser.py line 100 bind-mounts {ROOT}:{ROOT}:ro. All 24 steps were then enumerated: the 19 that need nothing special passed unaided, and the 5 that need namespaces, a Docker bind mount or libvirt are now gated. Both phase1 files were confirmed to carry the same step names and the same 5 gates. NOT verified: no run has executed since gating, so a green phase1 is expected but unproven.
